source_text: Non esse substantiam, sed conversationem, quae de sola voluntate contingat. Eos qui morbum conversationis suae propria voluntate sibi contraxerint. Hanc conversationem, quae accidens est, facillime posse a voluntate aegrotantium separari. Si evenisset malum ita ut non valeret ulterius a voluntate removeri, id est, quamvis accidisset, si ita accidisset ut separari ulterius a voluntate non valeret, merito dici posset substantiale quidem malum non esse, sed ipsam substantiam sine malitia quae accidit iam esse non posse. Si autem accessit et principium accessionis non substantiam habuit sed voluntatem, facile potest malum a substantia separari, ut et subiecta voluntati substantia munda possit per omnia possideri, ita ut nullius mali vel signa remaneant.

LS meritum=desert; Blaise without later merit-system

pass_b_english: “Evil is not a substance, but a way of behaving that comes solely from the will.”
“Those who have brought the sickness of their conduct upon themselves by their own will.”
“This way of behaving, which arises as something added, can very easily be separated from the will of those who are sick.”

“If evil had arisen in such a way that it could no longer be removed from the will—that is, if, although it was something added, it had been added in a way that made it impossible ever to separate it from the will—one could rightly say that evil was not a substance, but that the substance itself could no longer exist without the evil added to it. But if evil was added, and the starting point of its addition was the will rather than the substance, evil can easily be separated from the substance. Then the substance subject to the will can be kept completely pure, so that not even any traces of evil remain.”

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Glossary: avoid modern merit-theology; Julian means deserved outcome.
